skim: DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak passed 4,000 deaths as the fastest-growing outbreak on record kept accelerating, a Himalayan avalanche killed 15 Nepali workers readying a base camp, and the US logged its worst measles year since elimination.

Ethiopia and Eritrea severed diplomatic ties and traded embassy expulsions as the Tigray war hit its sharpest escalation since 2020–2022, the US sent a third carrier strike group toward Iran, and Putin warned NATO that touching Kaliningrad would mean “all weapons in its arsenal.”

Gold hit a fresh record near $4,218/oz and Wall Street rallied on a weak September jobs report that erased rate-hike odds, as Broadcom lined up $60 billion in debt to back Anthropic’s AI chip buildout and Oracle signed a $7 billion deal to lease 100,000 chips to Tencent.

Shubman Gill smashed 223 off 133 balls — the fastest double century in ODI history — to seal India’s series win over West Indies, the India–Pakistan Asian Games cricket final got underway in Japan, and F1 returned to Sepang with Charles Leclerc fastest in practice.

Modi personally video-called FlyDubai pilot Smit Machchhar to tell him “the whole nation is with you,” UK diesel prices hit a record 199.79p a litre amid Gulf tensions, and a tanker was struck by a projectile transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: DR Congo’s Ebola death toll passes 4,000 as outbreak accelerates
stories.body: The death toll in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak has crossed 4,018, with 8,300 confirmed cases — a roughly 48% fatality rate — across seven provinces, per Al Jazeera (Oct 2). Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya warned that “more than 80% of new confirmed cases were being detected among people who were not already on known contact lists,” while the WHO has called it the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak ever recorded. More than 2,000 patients have recovered, but officials cite weak infrastructure, ongoing conflict and community mistrust as the main obstacles to containment.

stories.headline: Avalanche buries Himalayan base camp, killing 15 Nepali workers
stories.body: An avalanche struck a crew pitching tents and fixing ropes at Himlung Himal (7,126m) base camp in Nepal’s Manang district, killing 15 workers who were readying the site for the autumn climbing season, per Business Recorder (Oct 1). One worker remains missing with rescuers holding out little hope; Tul Singh Gurung, president of the Nepal National Mountain Guide Association, said “the bodies that were recovered today are expected to be brought by a helicopter to Kathmandu.” It is the deadliest incident of the season, and comes as accelerating glacier and ice melt from climate change makes high-altitude labour increasingly hazardous.

stories.headline: US measles outbreak hits worst level since elimination, fifth death confirmed
stories.body: US measles cases reached 3,887 as of October 1 — up 228 in a week (6.2%) — across 47 jurisdictions, making 2026 the worst year for the disease since it was declared eliminated in 2000, per Contagion Live (Oct 3). A fifth death was confirmed in an unvaccinated patient in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, where 943 cases have been logged across 39 counties. Dr. Lori Handy advised hospitalization once patients show “dehydration or difficulty breathing, or measles-causing pneumonia where the child is breathing too hard to be okay at home.”

stories.headline: Brazil’s final presidential debate collapses as bomb scare hits Supreme Court
stories.body: Brazil’s last televised presidential debate was scrapped Thursday after both frontrunners pulled out: Lula appeared on a YouTube podcast instead, while rival Flávio Bolsonaro cited “censorship imposed by the electoral court,” per Al Jazeera (Oct 2). Separately on October 1, a suspect tried to jump the fences of Brazil’s Supreme Court in Brasília and threw a backpack onto a bus stop; military police spokesperson Raphael Broocke told AFP it held “only personal belongings,” and no injuries were reported. The first-round vote is Sunday, October 4, with 80-year-old Lula holding a slight edge over Bolsonaro’s son and a runoff possible on October 25.

stories.headline: Atlantic hurricane season heads toward historic no-hurricane finish
stories.body: Eight named storms have formed in the 2026 Atlantic season but none has reached hurricane strength — the first time in the satellite era that September passed without a single hurricane, per WUSF/NPR (Oct 2). Should the season finish without one, it would be only the third hurricane-free Atlantic season on record, after 1907 and 1914. Meteorologist Jeff Berardelli called the driving El Niño pattern “likely the most deviant climate event we’ve witnessed… perhaps a Grey Swan event,” though forecasters note October activity often shifts toward the Caribbean and Gulf, closer to Florida.

stories.headline: Gill’s record 223 powers India to series-sealing 400-plus chase
stories.body: Shubman Gill smashed 223 off 133 balls — the fastest double century in ODI history — as India ran down West Indies’ 405/7 to win the 2nd ODI in Guwahati by 8 wickets with 39 balls to spare, per Outlook India (Sept 30). It was only the second successful 400-plus run chase in ODI history, after South Africa’s famous 438-chase against Australia in 2006, and sealed an unassailable 2-0 series lead ahead of the dead-rubber 3rd ODI in New Chandigarh today.

stories.headline: India opt to bat first as Asian Games gold final gets underway
stories.body: India won the toss and chose to bat against Pakistan in the men’s cricket gold-medal match at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin, Japan, fielding Shreyas Iyer, Jasprit Bumrah and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in a full-strength XI, per Business Standard (Oct 3). The final follows India’s 124-run semi-final rout of Sri Lanka and is the first Asian Games cricket gold decider between the two rivals, who meet with India holding a 14-3 head-to-head lead in T20Is.

stories.headline: Leclerc tops second practice as F1’s Sepang return continues
stories.body: Charles Leclerc headed Friday’s second practice at Sepang in 1:37.528, with Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar just 0.099s back and Max Verstappen fourth after skipping a soft-tyre qualifying simulation to focus on race pace, per Sky Sports (Oct 2). Verstappen had topped FP1 ahead of George Russell, while Mercedes struggled to adapt its biggest upgrade since May and Lewis Hamilton picked up a €10,000 fine for impeding Gabriel Bortoleto — all ahead of qualifying later Saturday and Sunday’s race at the Malaysian circuit.

stories.headline: Gulf Cup last four locked in for Jeddah showdown tonight
stories.body: Saudi Arabia, unbeaten Group A winners with nine points from three wins, face Qatar at Al Inma Stadium at 18:55 local time, before UAE meet Oman — the side that advanced on a draw of lots over Iraq — at Prince Abdullah Al-Faisal Stadium at 21:30, per Africa Soccer (Oct 2). Qatar’s expected line-up features Akram Afif and Almoez Ali, with both Saturday semi-finals setting up Tuesday’s final in Jeddah.

stories.headline: Gold hits fresh record near $4,218/oz as rate-hike odds fade
stories.body: Gold extended its record run to roughly $4,218 an ounce on Friday morning — up from Thursday’s $4,177 high — as a weak September jobs report cemented bets the Federal Reserve will hold off on further tightening, per CNBC (Oct 2). Gold continues to draw safe-haven flows as a hedge against persistent inflation pressure.

stories.headline: Wall Street rallies as weak jobs report cools rate-hike fears
stories.body: The S&P 500 jumped 1.05% to 7,747.11 and the Nasdaq surged 1.64% on Friday after September payrolls added just 29,000 jobs — far below the 84,000 expected — while unemployment ticked up to 4.2%, per TheStreet (Oct 2). The 10-year Treasury yield retreated further as traders cut October rate-hike odds to roughly 18%; “There is zero chance for a rate hike in October now — September should have been a hold,” said Jamie Cox of Harris Financial Group.

stories.headline: Brent holds above $103 as US Navy escorts tankers through Hormuz
stories.body: Brent crude eased slightly to $103.37 a barrel — still up more than 56% year-on-year — as the US military said it is “guiding ships through Hormuz in broad daylight” to help double the volume of oil safely exiting the Gulf amid ongoing US-Iran tensions, per Fortune (Oct 2). Analysts note gasoline prices typically lag oil’s moves on the way down, a pattern traders call “rockets and feathers.”

stories.headline: ANZ dumps KPMG after 57 years over audit data-leak scandal
stories.body: Australia’s ANZ Group ended its 57-year relationship with auditor KPMG, barring the firm from its next audit tender after KPMG was accused of misusing confidential client data — including from Lendlease — to win corporate audit contracts, per ABC News (Oct 2). ANZ, which paid KPMG roughly $24 million a year, joins Macquarie Bank and Lendlease in cutting ties; a new auditor won’t start until FY2029.

stories.headline: Airtel Money prices £529M London IPO at £5.3B valuation
stories.body: Airtel Money, the mobile-money arm of Airtel Africa, priced shares at £1.96 for its London Stock Exchange listing, raising £529 million at a £5.3 billion (about $7 billion) valuation — set to be among the LSE’s largest IPOs in five years, per Business Standard (Oct 1). Trading begins October 14; backers including Qatar Holding and Mastercard are selling down stakes while Airtel Africa remains a long-term strategic shareholder.

stories.headline: Broadcom lines up $60B in debt to fund Anthropic’s chip buildout
stories.body: Broadcom is assembling a $60 billion financing package — a $42 billion senior-secured bank tranche plus an $18 billion junior tranche led by Blackstone, which is committing $9 billion of its own capital — to back the AI infrastructure Anthropic needs, per Yahoo Finance/Quartz (Oct 2). It underpins Broadcom’s pledge to lend Anthropic up to $42 billion toward its $125.2 billion five-year TPU leasing commitment, though Anthropic’s IPO prospectus flags that Broadcom’s dual role as chip supplier and lender could “compromise Anthropic’s access to the computing resources it needs.”

stories.headline: Oracle lands $7B deal to give Tencent access to 100,000 AI chips
stories.body: Oracle signed a five-year, roughly $7 billion lease giving Tencent access to about 100,000 advanced AI chips — hardware unavailable in China under US export curbs — through Oracle data centers across Southeast Asia, per Benzinga (Oct 1). About 30% of the deal is payable upfront, and Oracle shares rose on the news.

stories.headline: OpenAI and Synopsys to build “GPT-Synopsys” for AI chip design
stories.body: OpenAI and Synopsys announced a multi-year partnership to build GPT-Synopsys, a model trained to operate Synopsys’ electronic design automation tools and automate semiconductor design workflows, with revenue-sharing and joint go-to-market plans, per the companies’ announcement (Sept 30). “By helping them build better chips, we can build better AI and bring it to more people,” said OpenAI president Greg Brockman, while Synopsys CEO Sassine Ghazi said the deal brings “frontier intelligence to chip design.”

stories.headline: xAI launches enterprise Grok app for Microsoft Intune users
stories.body: xAI released “Grok for Intune,” a dedicated enterprise iOS app that plugs into Microsoft Intune’s mobile management so IT departments can deploy Grok’s chat, image and video tools under corporate data-protection policies, per 9to5Mac (Oct 1). The launch mirrors OpenAI’s earlier enterprise-app push and requires work-email sign-in with no in-app purchases.

stories.headline: Ethiopia and Eritrea sever ties as Tigray war escalates
stories.body: Ethiopia closed its embassy in Asmara and gave ten Eritrean diplomats, including the chargé d’affaires, 48 hours to leave, accusing Asmara of “direct and indirect acts of hostility and belligerence”; Eritrea said it “has no option but to reciprocate in kind and sever all diplomatic ties,” per Vanguard (Oct 2). The rupture follows Tigrayan forces seizing airports in Mekelle, Axum and Shire and pushing into Afar and Amhara, while government troops recaptured the town of Alamata on Sept 28 — the sharpest escalation since the 2020–2022 Tigray war, per Al Jazeera (Oct 2).

stories.headline: Pentagon sends third carrier toward Iran as Trump threatens new strikes
stories.body: The U.S. Navy is dispatching the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group from San Diego to join the USS George Washington already in the Gulf, with a third carrier due by late November and roughly 9,000–10,000 additional sailors and Marines — including 2,000-plus from the Makin Island Marine Expeditionary Unit — pushing total U.S. forces in the region past 50,000, per Al Jazeera (Oct 2). Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said forces are “ready to go” if Trump orders new strikes, while Trump told Time Iran will “do something very proper and smart, or they won’t be around very long.”

stories.headline: Putin threatens ‘all weapons’ response if NATO touches Kaliningrad
stories.body: Vladimir Putin said Russia “has no plans to attack European countries” but would “respond to aggression with all weapons in its arsenal” if NATO moved to isolate the Kaliningrad exclave — reiterating a Sept 30 warning that Moscow would deploy its “entire arsenal,” including nuclear weapons, per Business Standard (Oct 2). NATO fired back that Russia should stop its “increasingly reckless behaviour” and “irresponsible nuclear rhetoric,” insisting its exercises near the exclave remain purely defensive.

stories.headline: Russia pummels Ukraine’s power grid, killing seven as winter nears
stories.body: Russia fired nearly 190 drones and ballistic missiles overnight — 155 drones and five missiles were shot down — hitting energy infrastructure in five regions and killing seven people, including a child, per ABC News (Oct 1). Kyiv and three surrounding regions saw their first emergency power cuts since spring, halting trams and trolleybuses; PM Sergii Koretskyi said “Russia has escalated to massive strikes on energy infrastructure,” while Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called the barrage a “deliberate” distraction from battlefield losses.

stories.headline: Gaza death toll since ‘ceasefire’ passes 1,400 as drone kills father in tent
stories.body: An Israeli drone strike killed Tamer al-Hamayda, 42, in a tent sheltering displaced families in al-Mawasi near Khan Younis, wounding three others, per Al Jazeera (Oct 1). Gaza’s Health Ministry recorded eight more deaths and 26 wounded in the prior 24 hours alone, pushing the toll since the October 2025 ceasefire to 1,439 killed and 5,052 wounded — on top of at least 74,040 killed since October 2023.

fixtures.headline: India v West Indies, 3rd ODI
fixtures.body: Dead-rubber finale in New Chandigarh — the city’s first-ever ODI — with the series already wrapped up 2-0.

fixtures.headline: Australia’s Tour of South Africa, 1st Test
fixtures.body: Five-day series opener at Kingsmead in Durban, the first of a multi-Test tour.

fixtures.headline: Gulf Cup 27 Final
fixtures.body: Winners of tonight’s Jeddah semi-finals (Saudi Arabia/Qatar and UAE/Oman) meet for the title at King Abdullah Sports City (Al Inma Stadium).

fixtures.headline: Champions League Matchday 2
fixtures.body: League-phase action resumes after the opening round played in mid-September.

fixtures.headline: Bahrain Grand Prix Race Day (Sepang)
fixtures.body: Race day at Sepang, Malaysia, following Saturday qualifying — the first Bahrain-branded F1 race held outside Bahrain.

fixtures.headline: Singapore Grand Prix
fixtures.body: Next stop on the calendar after the Sepang weekend, under the Marina Bay lights.

portfolio.headline: Tesla beats Q3 delivery estimates despite year-on-year dip
portfolio.body: Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, topping Wall Street’s consensus estimate of roughly 461,974 even as the figure came in about 2% below last year’s record quarter. Energy storage deployments reached 13.7 GWh, up roughly 10% year-on-year but short of analyst expectations near 15.9 GWh, per Electrek (Oct 2).

portfolio.headline: Arm rallies on AI-infrastructure rotation as analysts reaffirm buy ratings
portfolio.body: Analysts covering Arm Holdings maintained Buy ratings with an average price target near $284.78 a share, as asset managers rotated back into AI-infrastructure names tied to custom cloud-chip designs built on Arm’s architecture, per TradingKey (Oct 2). Commentary also flagged a recent CFO share sale and ongoing litigation with Qualcomm as risks investors are watching.

portfolio.headline: Oracle director discloses $3.5 million share purchase
portfolio.body: Oracle board member Stephen Rusckowski disclosed a purchase of 25,000 shares worth roughly $3.48 million in a Form 4 filing, flagged by commentators as a vote of confidence in the company’s direction, per Benzinga (Oct 2). The filing lands as Oracle continues building out AI cloud capacity under the five-year compute-lease agreement with Tencent it signed this week.

portfolio.headline: Twilio’s S&P 500 entry set for October 6
portfolio.body: S&P Dow Jones Indices confirmed Twilio will join the S&P 500 before trading opens on October 6, 2026, replacing Warner Bros. Discovery, with FormFactor moving up to fill Twilio’s vacated spot in the S&P MidCap 400, per the announcement (Oct 2). The index move follows a quarter in which Twilio reported $1.50 billion in revenue, up 22% year-on-year.

portfolio.headline: Fubo launches ‘My Local Sports’ add-on; Wedbush reiterates outperform
portfolio.body: Fubo rolled out My Local Sports, a new add-on letting subscribers in select markets bundle regional sports networks onto a Fubo Sports plan, priced at $54.99 a month before rising to $64.99 after an introductory period. Wedbush has reiterated an Outperform rating with a $19 price target on the stock, above the ten-analyst consensus average of $16.83, per the report (Oct 1).

portfolio.headline: RBI approves Anup Bagchi as HDFC Bank’s next CEO
portfolio.body: India’s central bank has approved Anup Bagchi as HDFC Bank’s next managing director and chief executive officer, confirming a three-year term effective October 27, 2026, as he succeeds Sashidhar Jagdishan, per the report (Oct 2). The bank also appointed him an additional director effective October 2, pending shareholder approval, as it manages post-merger margin pressure, with net interest margin at 3.26% versus 3.38% the prior quarter.

stories.headline: Modi video-calls pilot Smit Machchhar: ‘Get better, the nation is with you’
stories.body: PM Narendra Modi spoke directly with Captain Smit Machchhar for the first time since the FlyDubai cockpit attack — having previously only called his wife and parents — telling the hospitalised pilot, “Get better and healthy, the whole nation is with you,” per WION and CBS News (Oct 2). Machchhar, recovering in Abu Dhabi from stab wounds, recounted the ordeal to Modi: “I was fighting for my life… I managed to open the door, and then everyone else came in.” Officials said Modi “applauded his courage” during the call.

stories.headline: Omani co-pilot held in Saudi Arabia; Netanyahu cites ‘Islamist radical indoctrination’
stories.body: Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu said the Omani co-pilot accused of attacking Captain Machchhar “underwent Islamist radical indoctrination” and was suicidal, reportedly shouting “Kill me, kill me” after being overpowered, per WION (Oct 1). Netanyahu said the suspect is currently held in Saudi Arabia and will be moved “very quickly” to Dubai for interrogation, with Israel joining the probe into possible Iran links or accomplices: “We’ll join the interrogation and find out what happened there exactly.”

stories.headline: Over 700 detained as AAP leaders defy Section 163 at Jantar Mantar
stories.body: Delhi Police detained more than 700 protesters — including AAP’s Saurabh Bharadwaj, Atishi, Sanjeev Jha and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh — at Friday’s Jantar Mantar rally against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, per WION (Oct 2). Singh staged a sit-in after being blocked en route to Parliament, protesting, “I am a Member of Parliament… How can you stop me?”, as Section 163 of the BNSS banned assemblies of five or more across central Delhi.

stories.headline: Five arrested, bailed over RAF Fairford plot as Iran rejects ‘Iranophobia’ claim
stories.body: British police arrested five men near RAF Fairford on suspicion of terrorism and explosives offences — finding only petrol in their vehicles, no explosives — before releasing them on bail, per Al Jazeera (Oct 1). PM Andy Burnham maintained there are “strong indications” of Iranian involvement in the “ongoing, complex and serious police investigation,” while Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed the claims as the UK “barking up the wrong tree” and “Iranophobia propaganda.”

stories.headline: Chagos deal stalls further as Trump calls treaty ‘an act of great stupidity’
stories.body: The UK-Mauritius sovereignty treaty remains stuck after Downing Street told Parliament in April its implementing legislation would not pass during the current session, with US President Trump branding the deal “an act of great stupidity” over fears it weakens protection of the Diego Garcia base, per Al Jazeera (Oct 2). Burnham has pledged to work with Mauritius and Washington “on a way forward” after Mauritian PM Navin Ramgoolam visited London on September 26, but Chagossian advocate Olivier Bancoult said his group remains “unshaken by Trump’s interference.”

stories.headline: UK diesel hits record 199.79p/litre as Trump dangles reserve release
stories.body: Britain joined Ireland, France and Italy in emergency talks with Brussels on releasing diesel stockpiles after UK pump prices hit a record 199.79p a litre, edging past the June 2022 high, per ITV News (Oct 2). Trump said of tapping US reserves, “We may do that. They have some diesel. The prices are coming down,” while a UK government spokesperson said Britain has “a diverse and resilient supply” of fuels — notable since the UK imports 55% of its diesel, nearly a third of that from the US.

stories.headline: Tanker struck by projectile in Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO confirms
stories.body: A tanker transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was struck by an unidentified projectile, its captain reporting a small fire and blackout onboard, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations Centre cited by The Peninsula Qatar (Oct 2). UKMTO said the fire was extinguished and the vessel continued underway with “no reports of injuries or environmental impact”; no group has claimed responsibility.

stories.headline: Qatar condemns Houthi strike near Prophet’s Mosque as breach of Saudi sovereignty
stories.body: Qatar’s Foreign Ministry strongly condemned a Houthi attack on a power distribution station serving the Prophet’s Mosque in Madinah, calling it “a serious violation of the sanctity of Islamic holy sites” and “a flagrant violation of Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty,” per The Peninsula Qatar (Oct 2). Doha voiced “full solidarity with the sisterly Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” reaffirming that “Saudi Arabia’s security is an integral part of Qatar’s security and the collective security framework” of the GCC.

doha_events.headline: Geekend 2026 wraps up at Lusail’s Geekdom Building
doha_events.body: Doha Film Institute’s annual pop-culture festival runs its final day today, October 3, at the Geekdom Building on Lusail Boulevard, with gaming competitions, cosplay, a Catan Championship regional final, art workshops and a Japanese Embassy kimono activation. Day passes are around QAR 25, per Qatar Living (Oct 1) and Marhaba Qatar (Sept 29).

doha_events.headline: Candlelight: Vivaldi’s Four Seasons at Four Seasons Hotel Doha
doha_events.body: The Qatar String Quartet performs Vivaldi’s Four Seasons and La Folia by candlelight tonight, October 3, at 9:00 PM at the Four Seasons Hotel Doha on The Corniche. Tickets range from QAR 250 to QAR 400 depending on seating zone, per Fever (accessed Oct 3).

doha_events.headline: ExxonMobil STEAM Festival continues at National Museum of Qatar
doha_events.body: A hands-on science and technology festival for families runs through November 28 in Temporary Exhibitions Gallery 2 at the National Museum of Qatar, with a STEAM Lab, navigation workshops and teen AR sessions; weekend family slots run alongside weekday school visits. Entry is QAR 10, per Qatar Living (Oct 1) and Marhaba Qatar (Aug 30).

doha_events.headline: Zinatha Women’s Shopping Festival — still running
doha_events.body: The 9th edition of this women-only shopping showcase continues at Al Hazm Galleria through October 7, open 10:00 AM–11:00 PM daily, with fashion, beauty, accessories and lifestyle brands and free registration. Per Qatar Living (Oct 1).

doha_events.headline: Savage Line obstacle race hits West Walk today
doha_events.body: An obstacle-course race spanning roughly 200–250m takes over West Walk in Al Rayyan today, October 3, from 10:00 AM to 8:00 PM, free for spectators with paid athlete registration, per Qatar Living (Oct 1) and The Peninsula Qatar (Sept 30).
